title: Scott Logic carries the strongest documented open-source ethos of any firm in the corpus
content:
The evidence recorded for Scott Logic is unusually concrete: a permissive open-source policy, a public GitHub organisation, a fifteen-year engineering blog, FINOS membership with the CTO on the board and leading a Technical Steering Committee, and FDC3 interoperability standards work. The verdict — the strongest documented ethos of any firm researched — rests on documentation rather than on declared intent.

The distinction matters because open-source enthusiasm is cheap to claim. Board-level involvement in a foundation and fifteen years of public writing are commitments with a cost and a history, which is what makes them evidence. FDC3 adds a second property: the firm already builds on open interoperability standards, so a component defined by a shared schema is a familiar object rather than an unusual request.

The firm is also recorded as technology-agnostic, which cuts both ways. There is no incumbent platform occupying the slot a record layer would fill — the disqualifier that removes several other leads in the corpus — but there is equally no product line whose gap makes the case automatically. The argument has to be made on merit, to an audience unusually well equipped to evaluate it.
